coaching.title: Recovery 5 mi + 600 ft (B2B Day 2)
coaching.message: Day two of the back-to-back — 5 miles, ~600 ft, and the only goal is to flush yesterday's 22/3,200. Zone 1 to low Zone 2, HR 120-138, nose-breathing easy. You're at 3,400m in Cusco, so your HR will read 10-15 bpm high for the effort — trust the breath, not the watch, and let the pace be embarrassingly slow. Walk the first 5 minutes if the legs are stiff. Power hike anything that spikes your breathing. This altitude block is free Julian Alps currency: 32 days out, running tired legs in thin air is exactly the adaptation that makes 2,500m of alpine vert feel manageable. Do not race this run.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You're still refilling from a 22-miler, so today is about replacement, not restriction. Target 400-500g carbs across the day — glycogen after a long alpine effort takes a full 48 hours to restore. Pre-run: 30-40g easy carbs (banana, white toast, or a gel) even though it's short; running fasted on depleted legs at altitude is a bad trade. Skip in-run fuel unless you go past 45 minutes. Post-run within 45 minutes: 30-40g protein plus 60-80g carbs. Altitude increases fluid loss and iron demand — push 3.5-4L water with electrolytes today, and get iron-rich food in (Cusco makes this easy: lomo, quinoa, lentils, eggs). Anti-inflammatory add-ons: tart cherry, berries, ginger.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Legs are in eccentric-damage repair from 3,200 ft of descending, so protect the downhill muscles. Ten minutes of calf, quad, and glute foam rolling tonight — slow, no aggression on sore quads. Legs up the wall for 10 minutes before bed. Sleep target 8-9 hours; at 3,400m your sleep architecture takes a hit, so give yourself the extra hour of runway rather than fighting for it. No hard lifting, no pole, no tempo pilates today. If soreness is still above 4/10 tomorrow morning, that's real data — take the recovery, don't push the next quality session.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: 32 days to Kranjska Gora. You're at the top of the mountain of work — this is the last heavy block before the taper, and the back-to-back you just closed is the single best predictor of how mile 26 feels in the Alps. The value today isn't the 5 miles; it's proving to yourself you can start a run on wrecked legs and finish it composed. That's the exact skill the Julian Alps will ask for. And you've got the SalesHive playbook review at 9:30 — get the run done first light so the day doesn't eat it. Discipline in the easy sessions is what earns you the right to be aggressive on race day.
